title: OPC-UA & SCADA Connectivity
contentStatus: PROPOSED title/content, pending DiFacto confirmation. Grounded in CDD Integration Ecosystem section (OPC-UA - data exposure and SCADA connectivity).

sections.title: Why OPC-UA Matters for Industrial Integration
learningObjectives: Understand what OPC-UA is and why it's widely used in industrial settings
Recognize how this connects to the SCADA layer introduced in L4A-M1
sections.content: OPC-UA is a standardized communication protocol widely adopted across industrial automation specifically because it allows different vendors' equipment to exchange data in a consistent way - without OPC-UA, every integration between different brands of equipment would need a custom-built connection. This is what makes MoRo's data accessible to SCADA systems and other industrial software regardless of vendor.

keyTerms.note: A standardized, vendor-neutral communication protocol widely used in industrial automation to exchange data between different systems.
A standard way for external software to communicate with a system programmatically, used here to extend MoRo's integration capability.
A system for monitoring and controlling industrial processes at a facility-wide level.
An industrial computer that controls machinery and processes on a factory floor, commonly coordinating with MoRo.

sections.title: How OPC-UA Exposes Data
learningObjectives: Understand the general concept of data exposure via OPC-UA
Recognize the kind of MoRo data typically made available this way
sections.content: OPC-UA exposes MoRo's data as a structured set of accessible points - status, location, mission state - that other systems can read without needing MoRo-specific integration knowledge. This is distinct from the direct REST API integration covered in L3B-M5: OPC-UA is specifically the industry-standard path for SCADA and similar systems to pull data, while the REST API suits more custom, application-specific integration.

sections.title: Configuring an OPC-UA Server Connection
learningObjectives: Understand the general setup process for OPC-UA connectivity
Recognize security considerations specific to this protocol
sections.content: Setting up OPC-UA connectivity involves configuring MoRo's system as an OPC-UA server (or connecting to one) that SCADA clients can query, with appropriate security certificates and access permissions configured. Specific configuration steps will be confirmed against DiFacto's technical documentation, but security configuration is never optional - an improperly secured OPC-UA connection exposes operational data broadly.

sections.title: SCADA Visibility and Monitoring
learningObjectives: Understand what SCADA-level visibility into MoRo operations provides
Recognize who typically uses this visibility and why
sections.content: Once connected via OPC-UA, MoRo's status becomes visible within the facility's broader SCADA monitoring - alongside other equipment, in the same operational view facility supervisors already use. This matters because it means MoRo doesn't require a separate monitoring workflow for facility-wide oversight; it becomes part of the existing picture.

sections.title: Troubleshooting OPC-UA Connectivity
learningObjectives: Understand common categories of OPC-UA connection issues
Apply structured troubleshooting methodology to this specific connection type
sections.content: Common OPC-UA connectivity issues include certificate mismatches, network/firewall restrictions blocking the connection, or permission configuration preventing a client from reading certain data points. As with other diagnostic work in this curriculum, isolating which category applies - is it a connection-level or a permission-level failure - narrows the troubleshooting path significantly.

sections.title: When OPC-UA Versus Custom API Makes Sense
learningObjectives: Understand the decision criteria between OPC-UA and REST API integration approaches
Recognize this as a design choice, not a universal rule
sections.content: OPC-UA suits integration with established industrial systems (SCADA, many PLC platforms) that natively expect it. Custom REST API integration (L3B-M5) suits more bespoke application needs - a custom dashboard, an unusual reporting requirement. Systems Engineers choose based on what the receiving system actually expects, not a fixed preference for one approach over the other.

questions.question: Why is OPC-UA widely used in industrial automation?
options: It's required by law in all facilities
It's a standardized, vendor-neutral protocol enabling consistent data exchange across different equipment brands
It only works with MoRo specifically
questions.feedback: Correct. OPC-UA's standardization avoids needing custom connections for every vendor pairing.

questions.question: How does OPC-UA integration differ from the REST API integration covered in L3B-M5?
options: They are identical with no meaningful difference
OPC-UA is the industry-standard path for SCADA systems; REST API suits more custom, bespoke integration
OPC-UA only works for battery data
questions.feedback: Correct. Each approach suits different integration contexts and receiving systems.

questions.question: Is security configuration optional when setting up OPC-UA connectivity?
options: Yes, it can be skipped for convenience
No - an improperly secured connection exposes operational data broadly
Security only matters for REST API, not OPC-UA
questions.feedback: Correct. Security configuration is never optional for OPC-UA connectivity.

questions.question: What does SCADA-level visibility into MoRo provide?
options: MoRo status visible alongside other equipment in the facility's existing monitoring view
Only maintenance history, no live status
questions.feedback: Correct. OPC-UA connectivity integrates MoRo into existing facility-wide SCADA monitoring.

questions.question: How should a Systems Engineer decide between OPC-UA and custom REST API integration?
options: Always default to REST API regardless of context
Based on what the receiving system actually expects
The choice doesn't matter - they're interchangeable
questions.feedback: Correct. The decision depends on what the target system natively expects, not a fixed preference.
